prompt: During an El Niño event, the normally strong trade winds blowing westward across the tropical Pacific weaken. What is the main ocean effect that follows?

options.text: Warm surface water that usually piles up in the western Pacific spreads back eastward toward South America
Cold water from the deep ocean covers the whole Pacific surface
The Pacific's surface water all flows toward the poles
Sea level falls equally everywhere in the Pacific

explanation: Trade winds normally push warm surface water westward. When they weaken during El Niño, that warm water sloshes eastward, warming the central and eastern Pacific and suppressing the usual cold upwelling off South America.
